subject.title: fix(auth-profiles): bound auth-profile JSON reads with size cap

question: Should auth-profile discovery preserve the existing ability to read a symlinked regular credential store while enforcing the byte cap, or intentionally reject symlinked stores as a new security boundary?
rationale: The PR changes a previously accepted filesystem shape into a silent no-credentials result; choosing between compatibility and stricter path semantics requires maintainer ownership of the auth-store security contract.

options.title: Preserve bounded symlink targets
options.body: Use a bounded descriptor-level path that retains existing regular-file symlink behavior and add focused regression coverage.

options.title: Reject symlinks intentionally
options.body: Keep the strict helper behavior only with explicit upgrade documentation, a migration/recovery path, and proof that this security boundary is intended.

recommendation.title: Preserve bounded symlink targets
recommendation.body: Use a bounded descriptor-level path that retains existing regular-file symlink behavior and add focused regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main auth-profile history ownership could not be established in the read-only review environment.
